# Agent Instructions

This project is a .NET transactional integration job built on the Intropy
framework. It reads files from a local Dapr file binding, publishes each one
onto an in-memory Dapr pub/sub topic, and processes them through a VETER send
pipeline that writes the transformed result to a second local file binding.

## Project overview

- Framework: .NET 10
- App type: Console job (no web endpoints)
- Runner: `Intropy.Framework.Hosting.TransactionalIntegration.Job.TransactionalIntegrationRunner`
- Pub/sub component: `pubsub` (in-memory)
- Topic: `orders`
- Source binding: `inbound-storage` (Dapr local storage, rootPath `/tmp/{{ .name | kebabcase }}/inbound`)
- Destination binding: `outbound-storage` (Dapr local storage, rootPath `/tmp/{{ .name | kebabcase }}/outbound`)

## Important files

- `src/Program.cs` - DI wiring and entrypoint that runs the `TransactionalIntegrationRunner`.
- `src/Configuration/Constants.cs` - component names, keyed-adapter keys, context metadata keys.
- `src/Receive/` - source listing and the receive pipeline steps (`Receiver`, `Enqueuer`, `Completer`).
- `src/Send/` - the VETER send pipeline steps.

# Intropy component manifest

Every Intropy integration component carries a project-level manifest at its root: `agent.md`, a terse project guide for agents working in the repo. It states the run command, ports, key files, and component names — the facts an agent needs before touching anything. This skill covers `agent.md` plus the canonical directory layout it describes.

## Project shape

A scaffolded component looks like this:

```
<component>/
├── agent.md                     # agent-facing project guide (run command, ports, key files)
├── README.md
├── local/
│   └── dapr-components/         # local Dapr component YAMLs (pub/sub, bindings)
└── src/
    ├── Program.cs               # DI wiring + framework registration
    ├── <Component>.csproj
    ├── appsettings*.json
    ├── Configuration/
    │   └── Constants.cs         # component/topic/binding/customer names
    ├── Ingest/
    │   └── Endpoints.cs         # MapPost + .WithTopic + StepResult → response
    ├── Model/                   # in/out records
    └── Process/
        ├── <Entity>SendPipeline.cs            # implements ISendPipeline<Context>
        ├── <Entity>SendPipelineBuilder.cs     # fluent builder
        ├── ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs     # AddXxxSendPipeline()
        └── Steps/                             # one file per Block subclass
```

Some blueprints add a `Taskfile.yml` (local-dev tasks wrapping the same run command) and `local/sample-data/`. When in doubt about where new code belongs, match this layout. Don't introduce parallel folders or rename existing ones — other tooling (and the scaffolder blueprint) rely on these paths.

## `agent.md` — the agent-facing project guide

`agent.md` is the project's guide for agents — package names, key files, run command. Keep it terse and concrete: bullet points, no prose essays.

The run command lives here (and in `Taskfile.yml` when the blueprint ships one). It's a plain `dapr run` invocation; what's load-bearing in it:

- **`--app-id`** must match `Constants.ComponentName` (which is also what gets passed to `AddIntropyFramework(x => x.ComponentName = ...)`). It's the identity Dapr uses for the sidecar.
- **`--resources-path`** points at the directory of Dapr component YAMLs (`./local/dapr-components`). Keep it in sync with the actual on-disk path.
- **`--app-port`** (when the component has web endpoints) must match the `--urls` port in the `dotnet run` part of the command. If you change one, change the other.

If you add a new Dapr component, you generally **don't** need to touch the run command — the sidecar discovers everything in the resources path. The component YAMLs themselves are covered by `intropy-dapr`.

Update `agent.md` whenever the facts it states change, so the next agent invocation has accurate context:

- Added a state store, a binding, or a second pub/sub under `local/dapr-components/`.
- Renamed a topic or component (bump `Constants.cs` and the Dapr YAML in the same change).
- Changed the run command or ports.

- **Don't point `--resources-path` at a path that doesn't exist** — the sidecar starts with no components and messages disappear into the void.
- **Don't let `agent.md` go stale.** A wrong run command or missing component listing misleads every future agent session in the repo. If the blueprint ships a `Taskfile.yml`, keep its vars in sync too.

19	
20	# Dapr components
21	
22	Dapr components in an Intropy integration component are wired in **two layers**: YAML files under `local/dapr-components/` (read by the Dapr sidecar at startup) and code references in `Program.cs` / Step constructors that use those components by name. The names must match exactly — that sync rule is the core of this skill.
23	
24	## The naming-sync rule (load-bearing)
25	
26	A handful of names appear in three places and **must** stay identical:
27	
28	| Name | `Constants.cs` | `Program.cs` / `Endpoints.cs` | `local/dapr-components/*.yaml` |
29	|---|---|---|---|
30	| pub/sub component | `PubSubName` | `.WithTopic(Constants.PubSubName, …)`, `daprClient.PublishEventAsync(Constants.PubSubName, …)` | `metadata.name` of the pub/sub component |
31	| topic | `TopicName` | second arg to `.WithTopic` / `PublishEventAsync` | — |
32	| binding | `LocalStorageBindingName` (and any others) | `new FileAdapterOptions(Constants.LocalStorageBindingName)` | `metadata.name` of the binding component |
33	| component / service | `ComponentName` | `x.ComponentName = Constants.ComponentName` (and `intropy.yaml` `spec.run.appId`) | — |
34	
35	Drift here is silent at compile time and shows up at runtime as Dapr **"component not found"** errors or **messages disappearing into the void** (published to a component name no YAML declares, or a binding invoked against a name the sidecar never loaded). When adding a new pub/sub or binding, update **all three** locations in the same change.
36	
37	## What's in `local/dapr-components/`
38	
39	A freshly scaffolded component ships two components:
40	
41	```yaml
42	# local/dapr-components/pubsub.yaml
43	apiVersion: dapr.io/v1alpha1
44	kind: Component
45	metadata:
46	  name: pubsub
47	spec:
48	  type: pubsub.in-memory
49	  version: v1
50	```
51	
52	```yaml
53	# local/dapr-components/local-storage.yaml
54	apiVersion: dapr.io/v1alpha1
55	kind: Component
56	metadata:
57	  name: local-storage
58	spec:
59	  type: bindings.localstorage
60	  version: v1
61	  metadata:
62	    - name: rootPath
63	      value: "/tmp/hello-world"
64	```
65	
66	`pubsub.in-memory` and `bindings.localstorage` are *development* components — they exist so a developer can run the integration without spinning up Kafka/MinIO/etc. Production deployment swaps these YAMLs for the real broker/storage flavours; the **component name stays the same**, so the code doesn't change.
67	
68	## The naming convention
69	
70	| File | `metadata.name` |
71	|---|---|
72	| `pubsub.yaml` | `pubsub` (or a more specific name if there are multiple) |
73	| `local-storage.yaml` | `local-storage` |
74	| `state-store.yaml` (if added) | `state-store` |
75	
76	The `metadata.name` is what code references via `Constants.*`. The filename is a hint; the metadata name is canonical. Keep filename and metadata name aligned to reduce confusion.
77	
78	## Adding a new component
79	
80	A worked example: a Kafka pub/sub component to replace the in-memory one.
81	
82	### 1. Add the YAML
83	
84	`local/dapr-components/pubsub.yaml` — replace the in-memory spec; keep the metadata name:
85	
86	```yaml
87	apiVersion: dapr.io/v1alpha1
88	kind: Component
89	metadata:
90	  name: pubsub
91	spec:
92	  type: pubsub.kafka
93	  version: v1
94	  metadata:
95	    - name: brokers
96	      value: localhost:9092
97	    - name: consumerGroup
98	      value: hello-world
99	    - name: authType
100	      value: none
101	```
102	
103	Because the metadata name is unchanged, `Constants.PubSubName = "pubsub"` and the `.WithTopic(Constants.PubSubName, ...)` call are unaffected. **This is the whole point of the naming convention** — swapping a real broker in is a YAML-only change.
104	
105	### 2. If the name *does* change
106	
107	If you keep the in-memory pub/sub for one flow and add a Kafka one for another (e.g. `orders-pubsub`):
108	
109	- Add `Constants.OrdersPubSubName = "orders-pubsub"`.
110	- Add a new `pubsub-orders.yaml` with `metadata.name: orders-pubsub`.
111	- Update the relevant `.WithTopic(...)` and `PublishEventAsync(...)` calls to use the new constant.
112	- Update `agent.md` to list the new component (see `intropy-manifest` for the `agent.md` conventions).
113	
114	### 3. Bindings — code wiring
115	
116	For an *input binding* (Dapr-side configuration triggers a Dapr → HTTP POST when something arrives — a cron binding is the canonical example), point the binding YAML at an endpoint route — the route name matches `metadata.name`. The endpoint handler itself is `intropy-endpoint` territory.
117	
118	For an *output binding* (code calls into Dapr to invoke an outbound side effect — file write, REST call, queue put), wire the typed adapter in `Program.cs`. The existing pattern is `IFileAdapter`:
119	
120	```csharp
121	builder.Services.AddSingleton<IFileAdapter>(sp =>
122	    new LocalFileAdapter(
123	        sp.GetRequiredService<DaprClient>(),
124	        new FileAdapterOptions(Constants.LocalStorageBindingName)));
125	```
126	
127	If you add a second binding (say `audit-storage`):
128	
129	- Add `Constants.AuditStorageBindingName = "audit-storage"`.
130	- Add `local/dapr-components/audit-storage.yaml`.
131	- Register a second `IFileAdapter` — but **`IFileAdapter` is a single-target type today**, so you'll need to register a keyed service or expose a new interface. Either prefer one binding per adapter type, or talk to the framework owners before introducing a multiplexer.
132	
133	For non-file bindings (HTTP, Kafka producer, etc.), use `DaprClient.InvokeBindingAsync(Constants.<Name>, "create", payload, ct)`. The binding name is the second arg's anchor — same naming-sync rule applies.
134	
135	### 4. State stores
136	
137	If a Transform step needs to look something up:
138	
139	```yaml
140	# local/dapr-components/customer-store.yaml
141	apiVersion: dapr.io/v1alpha1
142	kind: Component
143	metadata:
144	  name: customer-store
145	spec:
146	  type: state.in-memory      # swap for state.redis, state.cosmosdb, etc.
147	  version: v1
148	```
149	
150	Code:
151	
152	```csharp
153	// Constants.cs
154	public const string CustomerStoreName = "customer-store";
155	
156	// In a step
157	var customer = await dapr.GetStateAsync<Customer>(
158	    Constants.CustomerStoreName, customerId, cancellationToken: ct);
159	```
160	
161	`DaprClient` is registered in `Program.cs` via `AddDaprClient()` — inject it into the step constructor and pass it through the builder closure in `Program.cs`.
162	
163	## Does `intropy.yaml` need to change?
164	
165	Usually not. The sidecar discovers everything in the directory that `intropy.yaml`'s `resourcesPath` points at — adding a component YAML there is enough. You touch `intropy.yaml` only when the *run shape* changes (port, command, app id); that manifest is covered by `intropy-manifest`.
166	
167	## What not to do
168	
169	- **Don't hard-code component names as string literals** in code. Always go through `Constants.cs`.
170	- **Don't introduce `IOptions<...>` for component names.** They live in `Constants.cs` because the Dapr YAMLs need the literal value; an indirection just adds drift risk.
171	- **Don't put production credentials in `local/dapr-components/`.** That folder is for the development flavour. Production YAMLs live in the deployment repo / Helm chart.
172	- **Don't introduce per-environment YAML files in this folder** (`pubsub.dev.yaml`, etc.). The deployment pipeline owns env-specific values; `local/` is fixed shape.
173	- **Don't change `apiVersion` or `kind`** in the YAMLs — they're contracts with the Dapr sidecar, not stylistic choices.
174	
175	## Verification
176	
177	- The Dapr sidecar reads the components directory **at startup, not continuously**. After adding, renaming, or editing a YAML, restart the `dapr run` command. The code can be hot-reloaded; the components can't.
178	- Confirm the sidecar loaded the component: the startup logs print one line per loaded component (e.g. `Component loaded: pubsub (pubsub.in-memory/v1)`). If your component isn't listed, check the YAML path, `metadata.name`, and `spec.type` spelling.
179	- Alternatively, query the sidecar's metadata endpoint (`GET http://localhost:<daprHttpPort>/v1.0/metadata`) and check the `components` array for your `metadata.name`.
180	- Then exercise the flow: publish a test message (or trigger the binding) and confirm no "component not found" error appears in the app or sidecar logs.
